items.prompt: A mobile checkout retries POST /orders when the response times out; support sees customers charged twice for one order.
items.why: A non-idempotent create that clients retry → a client-chosen idempotency key stored with the response, so the retry replays it instead of charging again.

items.prompt: A nightly billing job runs on three scheduler nodes; at 00:00 all three must not start it at the same moment.
items.why: The issue is concurrent execution right now, mutual exclusion across nodes, so it needs a lease or lock. (Making the job idempotent as well is a good backstop.)

items.prompt: An order service writes the order row and must publish OrderPlaced to Kafka; sometimes the DB commit succeeds but the publish is lost.
items.why: Atomically 'write the DB and emit an event' on the producer side → write the event to an outbox table in the same transaction and relay it.

items.prompt: A shipping consumer reads OrderPlaced events with at-least-once delivery; after a rebalance some orders get two labels printed.
items.why: Redelivery to a consumer with a side effect → dedup on the event id (or upsert by order_id) in the same transaction as the effect.

items.prompt: A consumer keeps crashing on one malformed message, and every retry blocks the partition behind it.
items.why: A poison message → bounded retries with backoff, then park it in a dead-letter queue. Dedup wouldn't help, because it never succeeds.

items.prompt: A card processor delivers 'payment succeeded' webhooks at least once and sometimes 3-4 times; each delivery currently credits the merchant's balance.
items.why: Repeated deliveries of the same event → record the processor's event id under a unique constraint with the ledger write, and skip ids already seen.

items.prompt: Two admins edit the same product description at once and the second save silently overwrites the first.
items.why: Different writers clobbering each other (lost update) → a version check on write. These are two different requests, not a retried one.

items.prompt: A click-tracking pipeline must bill advertisers exactly once per click, although browsers resend beacons and the stream is replayed after failures.
items.why: Duplicate events and replay with an exactly-once requirement → a trusted click id deduped within a window longer than the replay horizon. Chunking-dedup is about file content blocks, not events.
